title: /billing-plans page is gated behind billing.read via PermissionGate; unauthorized users see Access Denied
preconditions: User has no billing.read permission (NORMAL_USER without CUSTOMER_BILLING_ADMIN role)
steps: Log in as the unprivileged user
Navigate directly to /billing-plans
expectedResult: PermissionGate renders the fallback 'Access Denied' page ('You don't have permission to view this page. Contact your organization admin to request access.') rather than any billing data.

title: /billing page (the alternate duplicate route) is not wrapped in PermissionGate — verify it is not an unguarded bypass of the billing.read check
description: src/app/(private)/billing/page.jsx renders the same Overview/Plans tabs as billing-plans/page.jsx but has no <PermissionGate> wrapper in the page file itself — still true post-rewrite. Two parallel billing UI trees still exist (components/billing/* and components/organization/billing/*). This case exists to confirm gating is enforced some other way (layout-level guard, or the underlying API calls still 403) rather than being a straight bypass of the access control on the sibling page.
steps: Log in as the unprivileged user
Navigate directly to /billing instead of /billing-plans
If the page renders, inspect whether the underlying billingService/subscriptionService calls (getPlan/getUsage/getBillingProjects/current/usage) return 403 or actual data
expectedResult: Either the page itself denies access via a layout-level guard, or every data call it makes (GET /v1/subscriptions/current, /usage, /projects) is rejected 403 by the backend's requirePermission('billing.read') so no billing data is ever displayed. If neither is true, this is a live access-control gap between two nearly-identical routes and must be raised as a defect, not silently accepted.

title: GET /api/v1/subscriptions/current never returns another organization's subscription/plan data
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B) each with distinct active plans/tiers
Valid JWT for a billing.read user in org A
steps: As an org A user, call GET /api/v1/subscriptions/current, GET /api/v1/subscriptions/usage, and GET /api/v1/subscriptions/ai-credits/history
Attempt to influence the org context via any client-suppliable parameter (e.g. a forged projectId belonging to org B, if project-billed) to see org B's data
expectedResult: All responses reflect only org A's subscription/plan/entitlement data, scoped strictly by the authenticated JWT's orgId server-side — never by a client-suppliable identifier. Any attempt to pass an org-B-owned projectId does not resolve to org B's SubscriptionInstance (composition.resolve(req.orgId, {projectId}) must not cross organizations).

title: Stripe webhook endpoint rejects a payload with a missing or invalid stripe-signature header
preconditions: Valid STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET configured on the server
steps: Send POST /webhooks/stripe with a well-formed event JSON body but no 'stripe-signature' header
Repeat with a stripe-signature header containing a tampered/invalid signature
expectedResult: Both requests are rejected with 400 { success:false, message:'Invalid signature' } and no handler for the claimed event type is ever invoked — an attacker cannot forge a checkout.session.completed or subscription-status-changing event without the real webhook secret.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no Stripe webhook endpoint (or any webhook endpoint) anywhere in the current codebase to verify a signature against.

title: Webhook route consumes the raw request body (express.raw) before any JSON body-parser touches it
description: Stripe signature verification requires the exact raw bytes; if a global JSON parser runs first and re-serializes the body, signature verification would either false-reject every legitimate event or (worse) be skipped, opening a webhook-forgery path. The code comment explicitly calls out that /webhooks/stripe is mounted with express.raw before the JSON parser — this case pins that ordering. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — there is no Stripe webhook route, so there is no raw-body-before-JSON-parser middleware ordering left to regression-guard.
steps: Send a genuine, correctly-signed Stripe test event to POST /webhooks/stripe
Confirm the signature check passes and the event is processed
Inspect the Express app's middleware mount order to confirm express.raw({type:'application/json'}) is bound to this route ahead of any global express.json()
expectedResult: The correctly-signed event verifies and processes successfully, and the raw-body middleware is confirmed to run before any JSON body-parser for this specific route — regression guard against a future refactor accidentally reordering middleware and breaking/bypassing signature verification.

title: NORMAL_USER without CUSTOMER_BILLING_ADMIN/SUPERADMIN role is denied billing.update actions
description: Post the 8->3->2 system-role simplification, NORMAL_USER has zero org-wide permissions. Only SUPERADMIN (bypasses requirePermission entirely) and CUSTOMER_BILLING_ADMIN (explicit billing.read/update/admin) should be able to mutate billing state. Confirmed unchanged post-rewrite: subscription.routes.js still gates every mutating route behind requirePermission('billing.update').
preconditions: User has role NORMAL_USER only (no CUSTOMER_BILLING_ADMIN grant)
steps: As this user, call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests
Call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests/:requestId/revise
Call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests/:requestId/cancel
expectedResult: Every call is rejected 403 { success:false, message:'Missing permission: billing.update' }.

title: SUPERADMIN's blanket requirePermission bypass is scoped to isSuperAdmin(req) and does not leak to non-admin sessions
description: requirePermission.js grants full access when req.isAdminPortal===true or the caller has systemRoleKey==='SUPERADMIN'. Because this bypass skips the granular permission table entirely, verify the check is strictly tied to the authenticated user's own role claim and cannot be influenced by a client-supplied header/body field.
steps: Call a billing.update-protected route as the NORMAL_USER, attempting to add a spoofed 'isAdminPortal: true' field in the request body/headers
Attempt to add a spoofed 'systemRoleKey: SUPERADMIN' claim anywhere client-controllable (custom header, query param, body)
expectedResult: Neither spoofed field grants the SUPERADMIN bypass; the server derives isAdminPortal/systemRoleKey solely from the verified JWT/session, and the request is still rejected 403 Missing permission.

title: Disabling pricing_v1 for an org 404s billing routes without leaking whether the org exists or is merely unentitled
description: Confirms the 404 { code:'NOT_FOUND' } response for a flagged-off org is indistinguishable from a route that genuinely doesn't exist, so probing does not let an attacker fingerprint which orgs have pricing_v1 enabled versus which orgIds are invalid. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — the pricing_v1 feature flag no longer exists; billing/subscriptions routes are not flag-gated in the current codebase, so there is no flagged-off-org 404 behavior left to verify.
preconditions: Org X: pricing_v1 disabled, valid JWT
A syntactically valid but nonexistent orgId, no JWT
steps: Call GET /v1/billing/plan as an authenticated user of org X (flag off)
Compare status/body/timing against calling the same route unauthenticated or with a malformed token
expectedResult: Both cases return a generically-shaped 404/401 with no differing error detail that would let a caller distinguish 'valid org, feature flag off' from 'route not found' or 'unauthenticated'.

title: EntitlementBalance and EntitlementUsageEvent rows are never readable across organizations via /v1/subscriptions/usage or /ai-credits/history
description: Re-verifies the multi-tenant isolation concern from the deleted BILL-INT-009/SEC-003 against the new V2 ledger collections specifically, per the note that this class of risk must be re-checked for every new data model.
preconditions: Two orgs A and B with distinct SubscriptionInstances and EntitlementBalance/EntitlementUsageEvent rows
A valid billing.read JWT for org A
steps: As an org-A user, call GET /api/v1/subscriptions/usage and GET /api/v1/subscriptions/ai-credits/history
Attempt to pass an org-B-owned projectId as the projectId query parameter on both calls
expectedResult: Both calls return only org-A-scoped data (all instanceIds resolved are org A's). Passing an org-B-owned projectId does not leak org-B balances/usage-events — composition.resolve(req.orgId, {projectId}) must fail to resolve a foreign project rather than silently matching it, since orgId always comes from the verified JWT, never the query parameter.

title: A customer actor cannot submit a limit_override request or a 'custom' add-on with a raw entitlements payload to self-grant arbitrary entitlements
description: request.service.js's validateItems() explicitly throws 403 when actor.type==='customer' and (type==='limit_override' or an add_on item has code==='custom'/carries a raw entitlements field). Verifies a customer JWT cannot forge these fields to bypass the admin-only entitlement-grant path.
preconditions: Valid JWT for a billing.update customer user (actor.type will resolve to 'customer')
steps: Call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests with type='limit_override' and any entitlements payload
Call POST /api/v1/subscriptions/requests with type='add_on' and requestedItems:[{code:'custom', entitlements:{'users.active':999999}}]
expectedResult: Both calls are rejected 403 'Custom entitlement adjustments are administrator-only'; no SubscriptionRequest document is created for either attempt.

title: overrideClientTier and grantCredits reject an approverId equal to the acting admin's own userId
description: requireApprover(req.userId, approverId) throws SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED whenever the two ids match, enforced on both the enterprise tier-override and AI-credit-grant admin endpoints — the two most consequential unilateral billing mutations available to a single admin account.
preconditions: An admin user with admin:billing:enterprise and admin:credits scopes
steps: Call POST /api/admin/billing/clients/:orgId/override with approverId set to the caller's own userId
Call POST /api/admin/billing/clients/:orgId/credit-grant with approverId set to the caller's own userId
expectedResult: Both calls are rejected with the SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED error; no SubscriptionInstance override and no AI-credit grant is applied, and no audit_log row is written for either attempt.

title: An admin scoped only to admin:billing cannot create, version, or deprecate an add-on or entitlement definition — those require admin:billing:enterprise
preconditions: An admin-portal session with only the admin:billing scope granted (not admin:billing:enterprise)
steps: Call GET /api/admin/subscription-catalog/add-ons (should succeed)
Call POST /api/admin/subscription-catalog/add-ons with a valid new add-on payload
Call PATCH /api/admin/subscription-catalog/definitions/:key with a valid revision payload
expectedResult: The GET call succeeds 200. Both the POST and PATCH calls are rejected 403 for lacking admin:billing:enterprise — a read-scoped admin cannot mutate the catalog that drives every org's entitlements.
